newsitem.title: USA: Acres Gaming sees Q3 oper loss.
newsitem.headline: Acres Gaming sees Q3 oper loss.

text.p: Acres Gaming Inc said Wednesday it expects an operating loss for its fiscal third quarter, ending March 31, because shipments of its Concept III components to International Game Technology "will be well below earlier expectations."
Acres also said it anticipates that earnings and revenues for the fourth quarter, ending June 30, will be below its previous expectations.
Acres said shipments of its Concept III data collection and bonusing components to IGT have begun, and it is working to combine this with slot machine maker IGT's Smart System.

It said, however, that while the process of integrating, testing and obtaining regulatory approval of the combined systems is on schedule, the delivery schedule has been adjusted to coincide more closely with the commencement of IGT's shipments to customers.
Joe Huseonica, president of Acres, said the company was pleased with its relationship with IGT even though it had expected higher shipment volumes.
On other fronts, he said Acres was making progress in end-user sales of bonusing system games and in the development of proprietary games.

He said Acres has received regulatory approval for installation of its Hurricane Zone product in Missouri and the company's first proprietary game, BlackOut Poker, is nearing the end of the development and approval processes.
"We expect it to be placed in Nevada casinos during our fourth quarter," he said.
For the third quarter ended March 31, 1996, the company had revenues of $1.45 million and a net loss of $502,000, or $0.07 per share.
The company did not specify its previous expectations for the fourth quarter.
